findings.message: The keyboard path of the theft choice is never exercised end to end. apps/web/src/main.ts:194-196 installs a global keydown listener that maps event.code through chosenTheftType and sends choose-theft. It does not filter event.repeat, so holding 1 sends one message per auto-repeat until the server's 8/s cap (harmless, since the ledger ignores choices after settlement). Both Playwright tests (tests/e2e/theftLoop.spec.ts) only click the option buttons. The pure mapping is unit-tested (apps/web/src/rubbings.test.ts), but nothing proves that the keydown wiring in main.ts reaches the server. A browser test that presses Digit1 or Digit2 would close this gap.
findings.requirement: the key and click handling is extracted into a small pure function (key 1 or 2, or a click on option n, gives the chosen type), with web unit tests for key 1, key 2 and clicks on both options; `main.ts` is wired to it;

findings.message: Stale comment in tests/e2e/seaDuel.spec.ts (the tick-interval block added before the return to sea): it says the match game is 'one Phaser game (Phaser.AUTO)', but apps/web/src/seaScene.ts MatchGame now uses Phaser.CANVAS. docs/architecture.md 'Rendering' records the switch and the measurements (135 ms p95 with AUTO; 8.5/8.9 ms with CANVAS). The assertion is still correct; only the comment misstates the renderer under test.

rubbings-theft acceptance 3 requires the per-tick invariant ('no ship removed while its player is in the ledger') to hold in every integration test. tests/integration/seaDuelHarness.test.ts 'keeps both fighters on the server's state with 80 ms round trip, 20 ms jitter, 1% loss' runs a full grapple and duel through a real MatchRoom, but runScenario collects its clients with a plain push callback, not tracker()/expectRoomChecks. So room.invariantViolations and room.ledgerRefusals are never asserted for that match. The server keeps checkInvariants on, so a violation would only reach console.error and the test would still pass. Every other MatchRoom test (rubbings*, seaDuel, ledgerSeed, the harness draw, and match/visibility/admission via afterEach) does assert them.
findings.requirement: The restored `rubbings-theft` feature meets all of `features/rubbings-theft/game-task.md`'s acceptance.

findings.message: rubbings-theft's settled design puts sourcesPerIsland sites at each island's docks, 'reusing a dock if the island has fewer' (apps/server/src/objectives.ts sourceSites, docks[slot % docks.length]). The only test, apps/server/src/objectives.test.ts 'puts each island's two sources at its docks in id order', uses seaMap, where every island has at least two docks, so the reuse branch never runs. No test builds a map with a one-dock island to check that the dock is reused.
findings.requirement: The restored `rubbings-theft` feature meets all of `features/rubbings-theft/game-task.md`'s acceptance.
